addons.name: Multiplayer maps
addons.about: Halo 2's classic multiplayer maps, for Project Gravemind's matches online, on your network and in split-screen. The campaign doesn't need them.

addons.name: Halo 3: ODST
addons.about: ODST's campaign and Firefight, which Project Reclaimer plays too. A Steam DLC of its own: tick it if your Steam account has it.

mods.name: ChupathingyCE
mods.about: The original Xbox Halo, rebuilt to run natively on Mac, Windows and Linux: the whole campaign, split-screen (3 and 4 players on one screen fixed in its latest builds), System Link on your network and online games. It plays from your own Halo: Combat Evolved Xbox disc, not from the Steam game files.
mods.caption: split-screen up to 4 · from your Xbox disc
notes: players (its README, chupathingy.org and release notes, read 2026-10-22): the campaign from the disc's maps folder, split screen (the README credits a fix for three and four local players; no maximum is stated, so 4 is inferred), System Link and online games including online co-op; no co-op player count is published.

mods.name: Project Gravemind
mods.about: A community-made program that runs Halo 2 from your own Steam game files, with its own Halo 2-style menus: co-op campaign for up to 6 over the internet or your network, multiplayer for up to 24, and split-screen.
mods.caption: co-op up to 6 · 24 in multiplayer
notes: players (its README, read 2026-10-22): co-op campaign for up to 6 (not said how many of them on one screen; split screen exists), online multiplayer for up to 24.

Halo 2's add-on halo2-mp (depot 976736, in Steam's "MCC - H2: Multiplayer DLC" with 976737, the groundhog files): its marker lockout.map is where Gravemind loads multiplayer maps from (halo2\h2_maps_win64_dx11\<map>.map), not yet seen in a download.
source: no checksum file; each asset's SHA-256 is on its release page (GitHub's asset digest), which mods.py checks.

Tested 2026-10-21 under Wine Staging 11.18 + DXVK-macOS 1.10.3: it needs no arguments, DLL overrides or environment of its own. It finds MCC in the prefix's Steam folder, keeps its settings, saves and logs in the prefix's Documents and AppData, and, its readme says, restarts itself after each match (the library waits for the whole Wine session).

mods.name: Project Reclaimer
mods.about: A community-made program that runs Halo 3 and Halo 3: ODST from your own Steam game files, with its own menus: co-op campaign for up to 16 (up to 4 in split-screen on one computer), ODST's Firefight, Forge, and multiplayer for up to 128. Nothing you have changes.
mods.caption: co-op up to 16 · 4 on one screen
args: C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Halo The Master Chief Collection
notes: players (projectreclaimer.dev and play.html, read 2026-10-22): co-op campaign up to 16, split-screen players counting toward it, up to 4 in split screen on one PC; up to 128 in a hosted multiplayer game. ODST since 0.9.19: its eleven missions and Firefight, from one Steam DLC (app 1064272, depot 1064222), optional (the halo3-odst add-on); Halo 3's campaign and multiplayer files are required.

dllOverrides: opengl32=n,b is Mesa's opengl32.dll beside the exe (extra mesa): its menu needs OpenGL 3.0+, which Wine on macOS only gives core-profile apps. xaudio2_9=d: MCC's xaudio2_9redist.dll forwards to the inbox xaudio2_9 on Windows 10, i.e. Wine's FAudio, which crashes mid-match and sounds poor; disabled, Microsoft's own mixer stays.

env: GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe is Mesa's software renderer; it redraws the menu layer every frame, and LP_NUM_THREADS=0 stops its worker threads each pinning a core (menu idle about 440% CPU down to about 250%).
extras: spinfix is the d3d11.dll shim in the prefix (spinfix/spinfix.c); loopback the local network addresses it binds (127.0.0-3.x, 127.3.1-3.x); presets its tuned graphics settings (presets.py).

mods.name: Reach Renaissance
mods.about: A community-made program that runs Halo: Reach from your own Steam game files, with the Xbox 360 menus: multiplayer over the internet with a public server list, Firefight and the campaign.
mods.caption: online campaign, Firefight and multiplayer
notes: players: its README and release notes (0.1.8 to 0.1.24, read 2026-10-25) give no player counts and don't mention split screen; 0.1.23's scoreboard fits 64 players.

Runs under Wine since 0.1.23 (2026-10-24, "Steam Deck and Linux: Reach Renaissance now starts under Proton"); 0.1.19 to 0.1.22 quit when they found Wine (notUnderWine, dropped 2026-10-25). Set up and played on an Apple Silicon Mac 2026-10-24/25 (0.1.24, Wine Staging 11.18 + DXVK-macOS 1.10.3): menus, Armory, Settings, online Firefight and multiplayer.

source: SHA256SUMS.txt is signed (SHA256SUMS.txt.sig, the project's key, which its own updater checks); some releases also have MANIFEST.txt and Changes-v<new>-from-v<old>.zip patches for that updater. The zip holds one folder, ReachRenaissance, with its paths written with backslashes (mods.py unpacks those itself; ditto keeps them in the names).
depots: 1064226 holds the multiplayer maps (20_sword_slayer.map is only there) and copies of files 1064225 also has; both are needed: multiplayer is most of what it plays.

process: Reach Renaissance.exe starts the game as bin\host-probe.exe and the menus as bin\menu-overlay.exe (Edge WebView2) and bin\rr-browser.exe; the Mac library watches these processes within this install, since Edge's background updater can keep Wine alive after the game exits.

dllOverrides: vcruntime140...concrt140=n,b is Microsoft's Visual C++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime (extra msruntimes) instead of Wine's: its host slot 32 reads a size argument haloreach.dll never passes and, with Wine's memset's leftover register value, wipes ~92 MB of stack (crash 0xc0000005 about 4 s after launch; reported to its authors). d3dcompiler_47=n,b: Microsoft's HLSL compiler, MCC's own copy (Engine/Binaries/ThirdParty/CEF3/Win64, copied into the prefix by extra msruntimes): Wine's fails the menus' WebGL shaders, which puts the 3D Spartan into a lose-context-and-retry loop costing a core. xaudio2_9=d: MCC's xaudio2_9redist.dll forwards to the inbox xaudio2_9 on Windows 10, i.e. Wine's FAudio, which crashes when the menu music starts (the same fix as Project Reclaimer's); disabled, Microsoft's own mixer stays.

env: WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--no-sandbox is what its authors recommend under Wine (the sandboxed GPU process exits otherwise). The other switches the menus need (--in-process-gpu, --disable-direct-composition) are added by chromehoist: WebView2 drops them when the host passes them.

extras: msruntimes is the Visual C++ runtime, the Edge WebView2 Evergreen runtime (its menus are a WebView2 page) and MCC's d3dcompiler_47.dll in the prefix; chromehoist the proxy msedge_elf.dll in the WebView2 folder (chromehoist/chromehoist.c) that lifts Edge's content window out of the host process, since winemac.drv never shows a window one process draws inside another's (win32u update_visible_region, winemac FIXME "Cross-process child window Metal swapchains are not implemented"); presets its settings.txt seeded with fps=60 and vsync=on (presets.py: the engine renders 400+ fps uncapped). Linux (play.py, untested) gets none of the extras: Reach Renaissance offers to install WebView2 itself there, and chromehoist is for the Mac driver only.

Quirks: the menus are a separate window exactly over the game window's contents (drag or resize the game window by its title bar and they follow; they hide while a match plays); they stack with the game's windows and do not float above other apps (Wine on the Mac cannot order windows across programs, so the menus are brought back in front of the game while a Reach window has the focus); quitting from the menus (Cmd-Q, the Dock's Quit, the menu bar's Quit, the close button) or from the game's window ends all of Reach's programs; the intro video never plays (no H.264 in this WebView2); the backdrop idles at 12 fps under the menus by design.
